title: Pest fumigation management intervention monitoring and control processes

lessons.title: Monitoring fumigations on the job
lessons.html:
What you will do

In this module you take part in monitoring and controlling real fumigations under the direction of a registered fumigator. You will practise taking and recording gas readings, checking perimeters, maintaining site security, and supporting decisions during the exposure, aeration and clearance phases.

Practical skills to develop

  • Operating gas monitors and detector tubes correctly, including checking calibration dates and battery or tube expiry.
  • Drawing samples through labelled sampling lines and recording readings with time, location and temperature.
  • Plotting readings to see whether concentration is holding.
  • Patrolling and monitoring the exclusion zone boundary and nearby occupied areas.
  • Keeping the fumigation log complete and legible.
  • Reporting abnormal readings to the supervisor immediately.

Scenario: a falling reading

During a bag stack fumigation in a warehouse, the readings on the line near the east side fall sharply between two checks while the other lines hold. You report it at once. Your supervisor checks the perimeter with a monitor and finds gas along the east edge where a forklift has disturbed a sand snake. With protection and a standby person, the snake is replaced and the edge resealed. Readings recover and the exposure continues for its full period. The incident is logged and the warehouse manager is asked to keep forklifts away from the stack. Your quick reporting made the difference.

Never take short cuts

Never shorten an exposure, reduce dose or skip readings, even under pressure from a client who wants to start outloading. Refer such pressure to your supervisor.

lessons.title: Aeration, clearance and evidence
lessons.html:
Taking part in aeration and clearance

You will assist with aeration and practise clearance testing under supervision.

  1. Confirm the full exposure is complete and record the time.
  2. Check wind direction and keep the exclusion zone in place.
  3. Open the structure from outside and downwind first, as directed.
  4. Monitor the perimeter during venting.
  5. Test all spaces, soft materials and the commodity with suitable instruments.
  6. Record every clearance reading and compare it with the label re-entry level.
  7. Report readings above the level and continue aeration until clear.

Only the responsible registered fumigator issues the clearance certificate.

Evaluating effectiveness

Take part in post-fumigation sampling and incubation. Learn to recognise survivors and to report them. Discuss with your mentor what caused any failure, such as leaks, low temperature or short exposure.

Emergency awareness

Know the emergency procedure for each job: who to call, where the label and SDS are, and the rule that nobody enters a gassed area to rescue without breathing apparatus and a standby person. Hands-on first aid training by an accredited provider is required for fumigation team members.

Portfolio evidence

  • Fumigation logs you completed, with readings.
  • Concentration graphs you plotted.
  • Incident reports you contributed to.
  • Supervisor sign-off for monitoring, aeration and clearance tasks.

Key points

  • Check instruments before use and record every reading with time, place and temperature.
  • Report abnormal readings immediately; quick reporting allows leaks to be fixed.
  • Never shorten exposure or skip readings under client pressure.
  • Aerate from outside and downwind first and test everything before clearance.
  • Only the responsible registered fumigator issues the clearance certificate.

quiz.question: What should you do when a reading falls sharply?

Wait for the next scheduled reading

Refer the pressure to your supervisor and do not shorten the exposure
